qa.overall_assessment: User's two fixes (line 749 evidence-based is_codex_thread_id; line 1093 scoped HAPPY_SERVER_URL discovery) are CORRECT and address the reported catastrophic failure (claude UUIDs misclassified as codex → sessionDeath archive). However, QA + codex audit found 5 analogous bugs in the same flavor/scope decision surface that are NOT addressed by the user's fixes. Two are HIGH severity (codex auto-restore is currently dead code due to unconditional Claude .jsonl check before flavor classification; line 1057 daemon-wait loop still iterates HAPPY_HOMES globally in scoped mode). Three are MEDIUM/LOW supplementary patches. A sixth bug (restart_daemon scope leak) is CRITICAL but out-of-scope for this remediation cycle. QA verdict: warning — user's reported root cause is fixed, but the remediation is incomplete.

observations: Function now requires find_codex_rollout to locate a /root/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*-<tid>.jsonl file AND _validate_codex_rollout to validate its first-line session_meta payload.
5 validation checks all fail-closed: file existence, filename UUID regex, payload.id == tid, payload.cwd non-empty AND exists, parent_thread_id absent.
Old UUID-shape-based behavior fully replaced — no UUID-only branch remains.

Edge cases tested: CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR missing → fails to claude (safe); rollout mtime > 14 days → fails to claude (potentially false-negative for very old codex threads, but caller's Claude .jsonl check then fails too → safe skip); subagent threads (parent_thread_id set) → fails to claude (correct); UUID coincidence with rollout filename → impossible (meta_id check rejects).
Caller chain at line 1196 uses the fixed function directly: `local restore_flavor="claude"; is_codex_thread_id "$uuid" && restore_flavor="codex"`
Caller chain at line 1263 (recover_session) also uses the fixed function.

Edge case codex flagged: find ... -print -quit picks first match without falling through. If first match is corrupted, we don't try second. RECOMMENDED minor patch (Block A-style newest-valid logic) but does not block this cycle's verdict.
Loop now iterates `homes_to_restore` (the scope-filtered list) instead of `HAPPY_HOMES` (the global list).
Effect: when SCOPE_HOME=/root/.happy-dev, the server_url is read from dev daemon's PID environ only. Prod daemon's HAPPY_SERVER_URL cannot leak into dev restore.
Per-spawn HAPPY_SERVER_URL at line 961 (inside daemon_spawn_session) is independent and was always correctly scoped to the target $home's daemon PID — confirmed by codex finding #5.

GAP CODEX FLAGGED: line 1057 daemon-wait loop runs BEFORE the scope resolution and still iterates HAPPY_HOMES globally. Even with Fix B in place, scoped dev restore can be satisfied by prod daemon coming up (then dev gets silently skipped at line 1131 if dev daemon hadn't started). This is the SAME scope-leak class as Fix B but on an earlier code path. REQUIRED patch (Block B in remediation SOP).

additional_bug_sites.name: codex_autorestore_dead_code
additional_bug_sites.description: Claude .jsonl existence check (lines 1178-1183) runs unconditionally BEFORE flavor classification (lines 1195-1196). For any codex tid in session_dirs.txt, the Claude .jsonl path won't exist → continue fires → is_codex_thread_id is never consulted → codex auto-restore is effectively dead code. This is the INVERSE of the user's fixed bug.
additional_bug_sites.evidence_based_replacement: Move flavor classification to BEFORE session-file resolution; branch session_file resolution on flavor. See Block A in qa-output-recovery-script-remediation-20260515-085807.md for the precise anchor-based patch.

additional_bug_sites.name: daemon_wait_loop_global_scope
additional_bug_sites.description: The daemon-readiness wait loop at line 1057 iterates HAPPY_HOMES globally before the scope-resolution block at line 1075 runs. In scoped dev restore, a running prod daemon can satisfy the wait, then dev gets silently skipped if dev daemon was not ready. Same scope-leak class as user's Fix B at line 1093, but on the earlier readiness path.
additional_bug_sites.evidence_based_replacement: Move the scope-resolution block (lines 1075-1089) ABOVE the wait loop (lines 1054-1064); change the wait loop to iterate homes_to_restore. See Block B in remediation SOP.

additional_bug_sites.name: scan_codex_via_mapping_emits_without_rollout
additional_bug_sites.description: scan_codex_via_mapping walks CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR looking for the rollout file (lines 866-875). If no rollout is found locally (rollout_path stays None), the parent_thread_id check is silently skipped and the row is emitted anyway via `print(f'{tid}:{cwd}')` at the bottom. Defense-in-depth: snapshots can be polluted with codex tids that have no local rollout evidence — those tids will then fail validation at restore time, but they've already polluted session_dirs.txt.
additional_bug_sites.evidence_based_replacement: Require rollout_path to be non-None AND require successful _validate_codex_rollout (payload.id == tid, payload.cwd exists, parent_thread_id absent) before emitting the row. See Block C in remediation SOP.

additional_bug_sites.name: manual_recover_defaults_to_prod
additional_bug_sites.description: Manual `recover <uuid>` without `--home` iterates HAPPY_HOMES at line 1381 and lands on the first running daemon (default /root/.happy = prod). A dev session manually recovered without `--home` lands on prod. Operator-facing scope leak.
additional_bug_sites.evidence_based_replacement: Pre-check: if $target_home is empty, infer from per-home session_dirs.txt. If still unresolved, error out and require explicit --home. See Block D in remediation SOP.

additional_bug_sites.name: usage_text_019d_prefix_obsolete
additional_bug_sites.description: Usage text at line 1640 still references '019d... prefixed ids' — the OLD UUID-prefix heuristic the user replaced with evidence-based classification. Operator-misleading.
additional_bug_sites.evidence_based_replacement: Change to 'auto-detected via /root/.codex/sessions rollout file existence + validation'. See Block E in remediation SOP.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: restart_daemon function has a CRITICAL scope leak: Step 2 (line 1524) kills daemon PIDs across ALL HAPPY_HOMES (including dev and qijie), Step 3 (line 1545) pgrep-kills ALL happy processes globally, Step 5 (lines 1568-1576) restarts only happy-daemon + happy-daemon-jade — NOT dev or qijie. Net effect: `happy-session-recovery.sh restart` kills dev daemon + dev sessions but never restores them. This is a different bug from the current incident; should be fixed in a separate remediation cycle. See Block F discussion in remediation SOP.
out_of_scope_observations.recommended_action: Separate cycle. Either make restart_daemon scope-aware (--target dev|prod) or define restart_homes=(/root/.happy /root/.happy-jade) and gate kill/wait/restore on that list. Long-term: align with /root/bin/happy-restart.sh --target API.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: Global restore (no --home) waits on the first discovered HAPPY_SERVER_URL only. In mixed prod/dev restore, prod health can satisfy the wait while dev API is down. Spawn env remains correct (per-home read at line 961), but readiness gating and logging are misleading.
out_of_scope_observations.recommended_action: Future hardening: collect unique HAPPY_SERVER_URLs across homes_to_restore and wait/log per URL.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: find_peak_snapshot checks only the first home due to `break` at line 397. Scoped dev restore fallback depends on prod home having a fresh peak snapshot.
out_of_scope_observations.recommended_action: Parameterize find_peak_snapshot to accept target homes; remove the unconditional break.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: `running_raw=$(scan_running_sessions)` at line 1122 is assigned but only `pgrep -f --resume $uuid` is used downstream — `running_raw` is dead.
out_of_scope_observations.recommended_action: Use running_raw to skip already-running sessions; only kill orphans if not daemon-tracked. Pure optimization; not a flavor/scope bug.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: find_codex_rollout uses `-print -quit` to return the first match. If the first match is corrupted (jq parse fail, payload.id mismatch, cwd missing), validation fails and the function returns empty — even if a SECOND matching rollout would have validated. Minor false-negative risk.
out_of_scope_observations.recommended_action: Optional patch: switch to `find ... -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -rn | while read ... _validate_codex_rollout` to try newest-valid first instead of first-found. Codex suggested also removing `-mtime -14` but QA recommends RETAINING the mtime limit (user may have set it intentionally for disk-usage discipline).
